title: Sidney Arodin, Lazy River and credit for Stardust
summary: DeDroit says Arodin wrote Lazy River, and remarks that Mitchell Parish's role in Stardust is overlooked compared with Carmichael.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Who was Sidney Ayrton? Sidney Ayrton was a sax and clarinet player from Drew Holman. She was a very fine one, very good man. And he played up north somewhere. How I mentioned him, and I have mentioned him a time then, because he wrote Lazy River. You know, Carmichael has his name on lots of tunes, but for instance, when you mention Stardust, you say Carmichael Stardust. But there was a man named Mitchell Parrish who had a lot to do at Stardust, you know. But they don't say Parrish, because, go on, the other fellow is better known, you see.

But you know when I ask any musicians to hum for me the voice of Stardust, they don't know it. I like it. It's pretty good. You know. Yeah. I wrote it for Shockey, but they didn't even tell me thank you. I guess he couldn't play another one.
